title: Capstone: Auditing and Optimizing a Page

questions.prompt: Order the six steps of the performance audit workflow.

items.text: Verify (before/after in lab, confirm in field)
Guard with a CI budget and monitoring

questions.explanation: Set goals, measure what real users hit (then diagnose in the lab), triage by impact, fix the biggest bottleneck, verify, and guard against regression.

questions.prompt: Why measure field data before lab data in an audit?

options.text: Field data is always faster to collect
Field data shows what real users actually experience and how bad it is; lab tools are then used to reproduce and diagnose the cause
Field data measures the server only

questions.explanation: Field (p75, segmented) tells you what and how bad; lab tells you why. Judging by field keeps you honest, then lab helps you find and fix the cause.

questions.prompt: How should you decide which problem to fix first?

options.text: By user impact × reach — the biggest bottleneck for the most users — then re-measure

questions.explanation: Prioritize by user impact and reach, not ease. Fix the biggest bottleneck first, then re-measure because the bottleneck usually moves.

questions.prompt: Match each audit finding to the fix that addresses it.

pairs.right: Break up long tasks and ship less JS

questions.explanation: Each finding maps to a specific technique from the course — the heart of a good audit is matching the fix to the cause.

questions.prompt: Which are good audit practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Verify a before/after for the metric you targeted
Stop as soon as metrics look good, with no budget or monitoring

questions.explanation: Measure, prioritize by impact, and verify. Stopping without a regression guard lets the next change quietly erase the win.

questions.prompt: To keep an optimization from regressing, enforce a performance ____ in CI (and keep RUM running).
questions.explanation: A performance budget enforced in CI fails a pull request that breaches a limit, and ongoing RUM confirms the field stays healthy — together they guard the win.
